questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go on exchange in Barcelona because the university offered some exciting subjects that I could not take at home in Copenhagen. Besides, I've never visit Spain before. So my choice is also based on experiencing a new culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Barcelona is a beautiful, warm and lively city for an Erasmus student. However, the academic level is not that challenging (compared to Denmark), which gives you more space to experience the city. You meet so many other students from many other countries, which gives you the opportunity to expand your international network.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not hard- There are many groups on Facebook in order to find a place to live, ask for help about transportation etc. Also, the university in Barcelona (UB) is very helpful and quick to answer you whatever questions you have for them- for example questions regarding registration for the classes.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was by my self. But UB (the university in Barcelona) added me two buddy-friends in which I could reach out to if I needed help upon my arrival. I could use them during the whole semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was on my exchange on my master, and the classes on the master at UB start earlier than the classes on the bachelor. Therefore, I met my buddy-friends a month after I arrived and started on my classes.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Use Facebook groups to find a place to live- there are so many :-) I stayed at a place called "Career de Santa Anna" which is a huge apartment consisting of 12 bedrooms (just like a dorm).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Based on my experience, by living off campus I met a lot of people who were either working (internship) or studying. This gave me the opportunity to hang out with new friends with different lifestyles. Also, it gave me the opportunity to have different groups of friends during my exchange, and to be in a broad study environment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They make the process very clear and distinct

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you register from home, then you show up at the university where you register face-to-face- they make it clear how to follow the process and what to bring with you when you arrive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mails, and at the university you could always show up their office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very succesfull- as long you register before the deadlines they give you.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont be scared when the classes consist of student presentation and projects- It sounds a lot, but the teachers are actually very flexible and put an effort to give you space and extra time if there is too much study and work at the same time with the other classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses at UB are way more flexible

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way different- At UB you have to make student presentations, project/hand-in papers during the semester where all got evaluated continuously. For example, a project can count for 30 pct. of the final grade and a hand-in paper for 20 pct., where the in-class exam counts for 50 pct.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Public Economics I: Political Economy
2. Economic Geography
3. International Trade
4. Intertemporal Decision-Making and Temporal Preferences
5. Public Policy Analysis and Evaluation
6. Welfare Economics I: Education and
Social Policies

- 5 ECTS each

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Based on all six enrolled classes, I will recommend to future exchange students to take:
1. Economic Geography
2. International Trade
3. Public Economics I: Political Economy

- because they include interesting reading papers and hand-in papers to work on, and the content in each of the three classes is new and relevant that can be used in the future for e.g. bachelor projects and master theses. Actually, I am going to use the theories in "Economic Geography" for my theses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Running- the so-called "uni run".

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus group in Barcelona makes a lot of trips both in and out of Barcelona, where they give you the opportunity to see other sides of Catalunya. Also, I can recommend to join salsa or bachata classes (It is very funny and you also meet new friends there).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to the cities around Barcelona (for example Costa Brava, Girona, Tarragona and Sitges)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the citizens are very open and kind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go on bars, get enrolled in Spanish language classes, or start on dance classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything! (in a good way)- the weather is good, the food tastes delicious, and the citizens are so festive.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pollution...

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be your self and don't be scared to not meet new friends (they are already there and waiting for you)
2. Make time to also experience the city by your self (Barcelona is so special when you have it by your own at a local tapasbar or at the park)
3. Be careful with your personal belongings (there are many pickpockets)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personal development, indescribably good memories and long-lasting friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first week: when everything is so new for you.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No :-)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
